constantNames: A constant name is derived from the code or from the name the publisher gives the code, as source says, and never invented.
The source text is decomposed to its base letters, upper cased, and every run of characters outside A-Z and 0-9 becomes one underscore; leading and trailing underscores are dropped.
A name longer than 60 characters is cut at the last underscore at or before 60.
A name that is empty or starts with a digit is prefixed with C_.
A name a constant of the same enum already carries goes to the first constant in list order; every later one is suffixed with an underscore and its own code.
A code listed under constants overrides all of this. The nine VAT category codes are the only ones so named: their published names are sentences, and the domain API spells them as categories.
